subject: Encord <> [COMPANY] | LinkedIn Follow-Up
text:
Hi [NAME],

Hope all's well, congrats on the new role as Product Manager, great step up
from your time at FoodLabs! Briefly - wanted to reach out as I saw the news
of [COMPANY]'s recent Series A raise, must be an exciting period of growth
for you and the company.

Given your role as Product Manager, will you be looking to use same model
for all your partners or do you have to fine-tune it on their data before
delivering? From my experience working with AgriTech teams like Aigen,
Carbon Robotics or Four Growers, fine-tuning usually gives better model
quality but is more costly for ML teams.

We've actually developed a data curation / annotation tool that solves this
dilemma and we'd love to get your feedback on what we've built for our
autonomous pest and weed detection partners.

Not sure how familiar you are with Encord, we're a data development
platform built for advanced AgriTech computer vision teams to build better
models (~5 years old, 70+ employees & raised $50M+ funding).

Given your new position at [COMPANY] and the rapid growth you'll be looking
for from the recent Series A, I thought it might be relevant for us to
connect. Would you be open to a quick virtual catch up some time this week?
I'm wide open at 12pm CET on Wednesday or at 1.30pm CET Thursday. Let me
know if you're interested & I'll get a calendar invite sent over.
Alternatively, my meeting like is here
<[LINK]>
.

subject: Hemal Intro | Encord <> Max Planck Institute of Animal Behaviour - Follow-up
text:
Hi [NAME],

Hope all's well! Just wanted to follow up on a conversation we had with one
of the researchers at the Max Plank Institute, Hemal Naik. Given he's now
left, would you be interested to continue the conversation - Hemal seemed
to think it could be of interest for your lab given all the computer vision
projects you have ongoing.

I've attached an overview of what we discussed with him and why he thought
it was relevant - happy to walk you through it over a call. Why Hemal
thought it may be interesting for your lab given the research being
undertaken at the Max Plank Institute of Animal Behaviour was:
- The research conducted at the institute is looking to *analyse amounts of
video & audio data* (with data continuing to scale).
- Researchers are looking at a variety of *ontologies* (e.g. tracking tail
beats, head position, body posture): with Encord, teams are able to create
a vast array of ontologies with infinite nested attributes.
- Researchers are working across *multiple modalities* (e.g. image, audio,
video): Encord is a multimodal platform, well placed to assist text, audio,
image and video.

At Encord, we have no limit on the number of projects or amount data
annotated within Encord Annotate instead of running a per seat model, if we
can introduce the platform to the Institute, we can be leveraged at scale.
Additionally, we are the only platform to render video & audio natively,
and able to accommodate for high resolution 4K images meeting the needs of
the teams at Max Plank.

If you're interested, please feel free to book a slot in my calendar here
<[LINK]>
.

subject: [YEAR] Annotation budget
text:
Hey [NAME]​,

Noticed that [COMPANY] recently released new Video AI analysis tools for Basketball & Volleyball, and was wondering if managing annotation budgets was top of mind as you expand into other sports?

Many CTOs of leading Sports Analytics AI teams we work with (inc. Hudl, Veo, and Spiideo) were struggling to balance customer demand for new products with the exploding data annotation costs required to train new models. 

Using Encord, teams can annotate native video (vs. breaking videos down frame-by-frame) - an approach which has helped Standard AI to save over $600k on annual annotation costs following its transition from CloudFactory.

Open to learning more?
